tools.description: Place a scene on the in-world story clock (day_index, time_of_day, duration_days, precision), optionally marking temporal_mode (linear|flashback|flashforward|concurrent) and a parallel thread_key. Drives the between-scene chronology check, the intra-scene temporal_coherence check (duration_days sets the expected span; temporal_mode/precision suppress it), and the in-world-time context constraint that feeds the prior scene's end clock forward.

clock.description:
In-world placement of a scene or event on the project's story clock. Every
field is optional: a project that never declares story-time leaves them unset
and behaves exactly as before. Distinct from [`StoryPlacement`], which is the
structural (manuscript) position.

day_index.description:
In-world day index from the project epoch (monotonic, spans books).
Negative values are valid: the epoch is the story's opening, and
births, backstory, and timeline events routinely precede it.

duration_days.description: In-world span of the scene/event, in days.

thread_key.description: Parallel-timeline key; scenes on different threads may overlap in time.

RenameReport.description:
Outcome of a character rename: what changed and what still references the
old name. The search index (FTS + embeddings) and the character's own FTS
entry are refreshed as part of the rename; the records listed here are the
ones the rename could NOT update safely.

arcs_referencing_old_name.description:
Character arcs (of this character) whose notes or milestones mention
the old name.

canonical_facts_referencing_old_name.description:
Active (not superseded) canonical facts whose value text, JSON value,
or aliases mention the old name. Facts that reference the character by
id are unaffected and not listed.

knowledge_facts_referencing_old_name.description: Knowledge facts whose text mentions the old name.

old_name_kept_as_alias.description:
True when the old name was appended to the character's aliases (it is
not re-added when already present, or when only the casing/spacing of
the name changed).

scenes_referencing_old_name.description:
Scenes whose prose or summary mentions the old name (FTS match on the
active branch). Rename never edits scene text — the author decides
which mentions are historical and which must follow the rename.

rename_report.description:
Present only when the call renamed a character (`changes` included
`"name"` with `allow_rename: true`). Lists the records that still
reference the old name so the author can fix them — prose mentions in
scenes are never rewritten automatically.

word-count targets that disagree between reader_contract.style_notes,
the narrator voice, and style world rules) so a stale figure is caught
at update time instead of after chapters are drafted against it.

tools.description: Update a supported entity by record id. Character aliases are settable via changes {"aliases": [...]}. Renaming a character (changes {"name": ...}) is a controlled operation: pass allow_rename: true to move the name's uniqueness key, keep the old name as an alias, refresh the search index, and get a rename_report listing scenes/facts/knowledge/arcs still referencing the old name. Without allow_rename the rename is rejected. For entity_type=project, the reader contract is updatable via changes {"reader_contract": {...}} or the sub-fields {"promise", "style_notes", "boundaries"} (partial merge; unset fields are preserved); if the edit leaves the contract's word-count target contradicting the narrator voice or a style world rule, the response warnings flag it

allow_rename.description:
Renaming a character is a controlled operation, not a plain field
write: it must move the normalized-name uniqueness key, preserve the
old name as an alias, refresh the search index, and report records
still referencing the old name. Set this to true to opt in when
`changes` includes `"name"` on a character; without it the call is
rejected. Ignored for every other entity type.

tools.description: Run a structured consistency audit (includes scene_divergence and canonical_fact_consistency checks). Fast checks run inline. A deep check starts a detached job and returns status in_progress with a job_id and the deep checks finished so far; call again with the same project and scope to join or collect it. Jobs are in-memory: a server restart drops the job and the next call starts a fresh one, while per-scene deep-tier cache rows are reused.

budget_tokens.description:
Token budget for inline markdown trimming. Errors are protected from
trimming; warnings and info findings are dropped from the rendered
markdown when the budget would be exceeded. Has no effect on the
structured `issues` and `report_sections` fields.

deep_scan_offset.description:
Page through capped deep audits in stable story/urgency order. Keep the
scope and manuscript unchanged between pages; defaults to zero.

scope.description:
Flat scope specification that survives JSON Schema sanitization.
`scope_type` must be `"full"`, `"book"`, or `"chapter_range"`.

scene_order.description:
Optional single-scene narrowing (P2.1). Meaningful only when the scope
already pins one chapter — a `chapter_range` whose start book+chapter
equal its end book+chapter. Any other shape (missing bounds, or
`start != end`) with a `scene_order` present is an input validation
error. Absent (the default) it deserializes as `None`, so scope
payloads authored before this field existed are unchanged.

semantic_host_reports.description:
Optional host reports answering `prepare_semantic_continuity` requests.
Reports are validated and cached; no model call is made for them.

candidate_set_hash.description: Hash of the candidate set in the request.

version.description: Row/version hash, not a display value.

evidence.description: Exact supporting scene evidence, when the judge supplied it.

exact_quote.description: Exact scene substring at the byte span.

start_byte.description: Inclusive byte offset where the evidence starts.

semantic_mode.description:
Additive semantic lane mode. Omitted means `off`; P2 builds candidate
requests/coverage only and never emits model findings.

subjects.description:
Optional subject narrowing. Each entry is a record id of the form
`<table>:<id>` (for example `character:abc123`). When non-empty, the
check runs only against scenes that reference at least one listed
subject. Subject resolution mirrors `find_scenes_referencing` and
supports characters, locations, factions, religions, economies, terms,
plot lines, conflicts, themes, motifs, world rules, narrative
promises, and system overlays.

checks_completed.description:
Deep-tier checks whose results are already included in this response,
in completion order. Empty for fast checks.

checks_pending.description:
Deep-tier checks a running job has not finished yet. Empty when the
audit is complete.

job_id.description:
Stable identifier of the detached deep-check job that produced (or is
producing) this response. Omitted for fast checks and for legacy
payloads.

markdown.description:
Markdown rendering of the report. Populated when the input
`format` is `markdown`. Errors are listed under `## Hard
constraints` and are never trimmed; warnings and info findings
follow under per-validator headings and may be dropped if the
budget would be exceeded.

report_sections.description:
Per-validator grouping of Phase 4 validator findings. Each section
lists the scenes that produced findings, with positions, in
`(book, chapter, scene_order)` order. Non-validator checks (scene
spine, narrative promise, pacing, etc.) appear only in `issues`.
Sections for validators that produced no findings are omitted.

status.description:

`in_progress` when a detached deep check is still running. Fast
(non-deep) checks are always `complete`.

tools.description: Atomically commit scene prose with its author-declared continuity package, beat annotations, optional chapter summary, and writer cursor; supports dry_run, stale-preparation checks, and idempotent retries. Pass exactly one of full_text or prose_path. For long or escape-heavy prose, write a UTF-8 file under the book workspace (outside .spindle and dotfiles) and pass its workspace-relative path with optional expected_sha256; HTTP/secondary calls resolve it on the primary's workspace

inputSchema.description: Input for `commit_scene`, the single atomic write for ordinary scene work.

beat_annotations.description: Realized beat annotations for the scene.

items.description: One realized beat annotation committed with a scene.

summary.description: What happens in the realized beat.

book_number.description: Book number (1-based) for a new scene.

branch_id.description: Branch to write on; defaults to the project's active branch.

chapter_number.description: Chapter number (1-based) for a new scene.

chapter_summary.description: Optional chapter-completion summary, normally supplied for the final scene.

promise_events.description: Narrative promise events across the chapter.

context_revision_token.description: Composite context revision token from `prepare_scene`, revalidated before writing.

continuity.description: Typed author-declared continuity changes applied atomically with the prose.

canonical_facts.description: Canonical facts established in this scene.

items.description: One canonical fact established by the committed scene.

aliases.description: Alternate names that should resolve to this fact.

fact_type.description: Optional fact category label; `predicate` is used when omitted.

key.description: Optional legacy short key; used as the predicate when `predicate` is absent.

scope.description: Whether the fact is invariant, evolving, or conditional.

subject_id.description: Subject record id when the fact is about a specific entity.

subject_table.description: Subject table the fact belongs to (for example `character` or `project`).

supersedes_fact_id.description: Existing fact id this entry supersedes.

valid_from.description: Story placement from which the fact is valid.

scene_order.description: Scene order within the chapter (1-based), when known.

valid_until.description: Story placement after which the fact is no longer valid.

scene_order.description: Scene order within the chapter (1-based), when known.

value.description: Optional legacy value string; `value_text` takes precedence.

value_json.description: Structured JSON value for composite facts.

value_kind.description: Value shape (`string`, `number`, or `json`); inferred when omitted.

character_states.description: Character state changes established in this scene.

items.description: One character state change committed with a scene.

changes.description: New state fields; omitted fields inherit the prior state.

emotional_state.description: Emotional-state keys and their new values.

goals.description: Current goals after the scene; omitted entries inherit the prior state.

notes.description: Author notes about the state change.

source_summary.description: Short summary of what caused the change.

status.description: Current status descriptors after the scene.

character_id.description: Character record id whose state changes.

knowledge_learned.description: Character knowledge acquired on the page, including secret reveals.

items.description: One on-page knowledge acquisition committed with a scene.

character_id.description: Character record id who learns the fact.

fact.description: Short statement of the learned fact.

reader_visible.description: Whether the reader also learns the fact; defaults to true.

secret_of_fact_id.description: Secret canonical fact id revealed to this character, when applicable.

source_summary.description: Optional note on how the fact was learned.

narrative_promises.description: Narrative promises planted in this scene.

items.description: One author-declared narrative promise planted in the committed scene.

description.description: What the prose promises the reader.

notes.description: Optional author notes about the promise.

planned_payoff.description: Planned payoff placement, when one is known.

scene_order.description: Scene order within the chapter (1-based), when known.

planted_at.description: Story placement where the promise is planted.

scene_order.description: Scene order within the chapter (1-based), when known.

quantity_states.description: Quantity readings established in this scene.

items.description: One author-declared quantity state committed with a scene.

measure.description: Declared measure name, validated against the project scheme when one exists.

band.description: Declared progression band, validated against the project scheme.

change_reason.description: Why the reading changed, when it reflects a deliberate jump.

subject_id.description: Record id of the subject that owns the quantity.

subject_table.description: Subject table the quantity belongs to (for example `character`).

relationship_updates.description: Relationship trust/tension deltas established in this scene.

items.description: One relationship trust/tension change committed with a scene.

character_a_id.description: First character record id in the relationship.

character_b_id.description: Second character record id in the relationship.

tension_delta.description: Tension change applied by this scene.

trust_delta.description: Trust change applied by this scene.

timeline_events.description: Timeline events established in this scene.

items.description: One author-declared timeline event established in the committed scene.

placement.description: Story placement where the event occurs.

scene_order.description: Scene order within the chapter (1-based), when known.

dependency_tokens.description: Optional individual dependency hashes for detailed staleness reporting.

canon_snapshot_hash.description: Content hash of the branch-visible canon state for this placement.

plan_revision_hash.description: Content hash of the chapter plan and outline covering this placement.

scene_text_hash.description: Content hash of the persisted scene prose at preparation time, if a scene exists.

style_revision_hash.description: Content hash of the project reader contract, narrator voice, style rules, and active style profile.

dry_run.description: When true, run the full preflight and report proposed effects without writing.

expected_phase.description: Expected authoring scene phase before the run phase may advance.

expected_scene_version.description: Expected current scene version; a mismatch rejects the commit as stale.

expected_sha256.description:
Optional SHA-256 of the source bytes (file bytes, or inline UTF-8) for
integrity checking before the commit.

full_text.description:
Full scene prose. Exactly one of `full_text` or `prose_path` is required.
This text is persisted and never echoed back in the receipt.

generation_receipt.description: Optional provider generation receipt id required for explicit prose.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated key that makes retries safe; reuse with different content fails.

location_id.description: Optional location record id where the scene takes place.

prose_path.description:
Workspace-relative path to a UTF-8 scene prose file. Exactly one of
`full_text` or `prose_path` is required. The path is resolved by the
primary process against the folder containing `.spindle/`; dotfiles and
`.spindle/` internals are rejected.

run_id.description: Optional enclosing authoring run whose phase advances on a live success.

scene_id.description: Existing scene identifier; when omitted, provide the placement fields.

scene_order.description: Scene order within the chapter (1-based) for a new scene.

UnresolvedAlternativeEntry.description:
A scene stored on an `alternative`-type branch that is NOT the active
branch, reported beside (never inside) the spine listing. These are the
rows `generate_alternatives` produced; until one is promoted via
`select_alternative` it is not part of the active-branch spine and is
never rendered by `compile_manuscript` or addressable by position.

scenes.description:
The active-branch spine of this chapter, exactly what
`compile_manuscript` renders and the position resolver addresses.
Never contains rows from other branches and never contains duplicate
`scene_order` values.

unresolved_alternatives.description:
Alternative-branch scenes in this chapter that were never promoted to
the active branch. Deliberately separate from `scenes` so they can
never be mistaken for the spine or deleted by position.

blocking_continuity_findings.description:
Continuity findings (canonical-fact contradictions + retcons) detected by
the write-time gate. Error-severity entries are what would block the
commit under `BlockErrors`.

retcon_findings.description: Structured retcon findings surfaced by the write-time gate.

temporal_findings.description:
Intra-scene temporal-coherence advisories (deterministic prose scan).
Always advisory: every entry is `severity: "warning"`, kept in its own
field (never in `blocking_continuity_findings`), so a temporal finding
cannot block a commit under any `continuity_gate`.
